An obsidian fortress on a floating shard of volcanic rock, still warm and smoking from ancient eruption, its black towers rising sharply against a sky of orange cloud at perpetual dusk.
A fairy-tale palace of white stone and blue slate on a floating meadow, wildflowers growing to the very edge of the rock, the soft earth ending abruptly in a clean drop to open sky.

A drowned castle somehow afloat, its lower halls still flooded, long ribbons of seaweed hanging from its underside into the open air beneath, the whole waterlogged mass impossibly drifting through bright cloud.
A colosseum-shaped sky-fortress, its oval walls open to the heavens at the center, galleries and towers stacked high around the rim, the entire structure resting on a wide shelf of floating stone.
A castle of mirrored glass balanced on a needle of floating crystal, every tower reflecting the clouds and sky around it until the whole structure seems barely there, a ghost of refracted light.
A fortress-city built on the back of a vast floating coral reef, pink and white towers rising from the living rock, the reef's underside dripping long calcified columns into the silent air below.
A sky-citadel half-buried in a permanent ceiling of high cloud, only its tallest spires and banners visible from below, the bulk of its towers and walls hidden in white mist above the world.

A cloud-borne city of white towers rising from a vast plateau of solidified cumulus, its spires piercing higher clouds, streets and plazas suspended in open sky with nothing beneath but blue and wind.
